title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

errors: '{X,X'} modérée ⟹ {Fr X, Fr Y} modérée' should read '{X,Y} modulaire ⟹ {Fr X, Fr Y} modulaire'. Likewise 'Fr X ∪ Fr X' should be 'Fr X ∨ Fr Y'; by p.32's warning, ∨ is not the set union ∪.

Conditions (a) and (b) are not equivalent as written. 'X° = ∅' does not imply 'X closed'. They become equivalent only if X^• denotes something other than the frontier, or if (b) is read as a condition on X̄. Probably (a) means 'empty interior' and (b) means 'closed with empty interior'. In the tame setting these differ only by passing to the closure, using the tame fact that the closure of a set with empty interior has empty interior.
X∨Y = X+Y−XY is fine in characteristic 2, where − = +. The usual Boolean-ring formula is X+Y+XY.

The Boolean-ring translation requires all pairs to be modular, i.e. M a genuine Boolean algebra. With only partial modularity one gets at best a partial Boolean algebra, and + and · are only defined on compatible pairs. The page is vague here ('4) remplacé ... comme il a été dit').

ideas.what: Axiomatic poset of tame subsets with a partial 'modular pair' relation, a complement defined as the largest disjoint modular partner, and a closure operator
ideas.modern_name: Orthoposet / partial Boolean algebra with compatibility relation, plus closure; compare o-minimal or tame-topology axiomatics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partial Boolean algebras: Kochen–Specker 1967. Orthomodular posets: Birkhoff–von Neumann 1936 and the quantum-logic school. Tame topology axioms: van den Dries, Shiota (1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is advocated programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5), but this lattice-theoretic axiomatization is not published there

ideas.what: Frontier Fr X = X̄ ∧ X̄', with complement X° ∨ X'°, and stability of modular pairs under taking frontiers
ideas.modern_name: Boundary operator in a closure/interior algebra

ideas.what: In the tame plane, sets with empty interior are exactly the subsets of finite unions of admissible curve pieces
ideas.modern_name: Dimension theory of tame / o-minimal sets (dim < 2 iff empty interior iff contained in finitely many curves)

ideas.what: Boolean ring structure from the lattice: X+Y = (X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)', X·Y = X∧Y
ideas.modern_name: Stone's Boolean algebra / Boolean ring correspondence

ideas.what: Relativization of the axioms to M_{≤A} (next page)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's abstract framework for dissections is a poset with a partial compatibility ('modulaire') relation that holds for comparable elements. It has an orthocomplement defined as the largest compatible disjoint element, and De Morgan only on compatible pairs. This is essentially the structure of orthomodular posets and partial Boolean algebras from quantum logic, here enriched with a closure operator. That link between tame topology axiomatics and partial Boolean algebras / closure algebras does not seem to be made in the literature.
missed.quote: Considérons un ensemble ordonné M satisfaisant les conditions 1), 7) ... X+Y=(X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a point-free, order-theoretic axiomatization of tame topology on surfaces, closer to locale or closure-algebra methods than to the model-theoretic o-minimal approach. It could interest people working on point-free or constructive tame geometry, and on combinatorial maps or dessins.

missed.claim: The program of building 'réseaux' (maps or graphs on surfaces) from an abstract lattice of tame sets with closure is sketched here axiom by axiom (frontier operator, relativization). Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée', announced in the Esquisse, was never written up in this form.
missed.quote: Fr X ≝ X̄ ∧ X̄' ; (Fr X)' = X° ∨ X'°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete trace of how Grothendieck intended to found tame topology for dessins d'enfants. This is only modest novelty, since o-minimality later covered the ground.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual results are routine (boundary in a closure algebra, the Stone ring structure, the tame dimension fact). The mildly notable point is the unpublished choice of axioms: a partial 'modular' compatibility relation with orthocomplement. It mirrors quantum-logic orthoposets inside a tame-topology program, an unrecorded but not deep connection.
transcription_corrections: 'modérée' on this page is almost certainly 'modulaire' (as on p.32): '{X,X'} modulaire', '{Fr X, Fr Y} est modulaire'. Likewise p.34's 'connexe[?]' is probably 'modulaire'.
'Fr X ∪ Fr X' should read 'Fr X ∨ Fr Y' (the second X is a Y).
'(avec 4) remplacé enjointement[?]' is perhaps '(avec 4) remplacé conjointement' or 'renforcé'; illegible.
Margin note likely reads 'pour propriétés spéciales au cas modéré des découpages ... cf. Lemme 1' or similar; uncertain.
